title: Practice 2: Where to: в and на

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Давай перекинемся в ___ (картишки, acc. pl.).
exercises.prompt: Let's play some cards.
exercises.why: **картишки → картишки** (acc. pl.). Plural-only, inanimate; nominative plural картишки; declines like DLI's слова (hard stem): A. слова. Ending — (no ending) → — (no ending).  Declension: sg. — · — · — · — · — · —; pl. картишки · картишек · картишкам · картишки · картишками · картишках.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Отвернитесь на ___ (минута, acc. sg.)! Я по-быстрому переоденусь.
exercises.prompt: Look away for a minute! I'm going to quickly change my clothes.
exercises.why: **минута → минуту** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -а — declines like DLI's сестра: A. сестру. Ending -а → -у.  Declension: sg. минута · минуты · минуте · минуту · минутой · минуте; pl. минуты · минут · минутам · минуты · минутами · минутах.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Ты в ___ (пятница, acc. sg.) свободна?
exercises.prompt: Are you available on Friday?
exercises.why: **пятница → пятницу** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -а — declines like DLI's сестра: A. сестру. Ending -а → -у.  Declension: sg. пятница · пятницы · пятнице · пятницу · пятницей · пятнице; pl. пятницы · пятниц · пятницам · пятницы · пятницами · пятницах.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Кэнсукэ и Тодзи сделали всё возможное, чтобы прийти на ___ (станция, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: Kensuke and Touji went out of their way to come to the station.
exercises.why: **станция → станцию** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -ия — declines like DLI's армия: A. армию. Ending -я → -ю.  Declension: sg. станция · станции · станции · станцию · станцией · станции; pl. станции · станций · станциям · станции · станциями · станциях.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Джордж ударил его в ___ (живот, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: George hit him in the stomach.
exercises.why: **живот → живот** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a hard consonant — declines like DLI's дом: A. дом. Ending — (no ending) → — (no ending).  Declension: sg. живот · живота · животу · живот · животом · животе; pl. животы · животов · животам · животы · животами · животах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Том похож на ___ (обезьяна, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: Tom looks like a monkey.
exercises.why: **обезьяна → обезьяну** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -а — declines like DLI's сестра: A. сестру. Ending -а → -у.  Declension: sg. обезьяна · обезьяны · обезьяне · обезьяну · обезьяной · обезьяне; pl. обезьяны · обезьян · обезьянам · обезьян · обезьянами · обезьянах.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Дождевая вода испаряется в ___ (жаркий день, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: The rain water is evaporating on a hot day.
exercises.why: **день → день** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in -ь — declines like DLI's автомобиль: A. автомобиль. Ending -ь → -ь.  **жаркий → жаркий** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with день). Adjective type III, guttural (after г, к, х) — declines like DLI's русский: A. anim. = G., inan. = N.. Ending -ий → -ий.  Declension: sg. день · дня · дню · день · днём · дне; pl. дни · дней · дням · дни · днями · днях.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Мне надо на ___ (крестины, acc. pl.) двоюродного брата.
exercises.prompt: I have to go to my cousin's baptism.
exercises.why: **крестины → крестины** (acc. pl.). Plural-only, inanimate; nominative plural крестины; declines like DLI's слова (hard stem): A. слова. Ending — (no ending) → — (no ending).  Declension: sg. — · — · — · — · — · —; pl. крестины · крестин · крестинам · крестины · крестинами · крестинах.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Я знаю людей, которые каждое утро облачаются в ___ (новый, acc. pl.) проблемы.
exercises.prompt: I know people who get themselves mixed up in new problems every morning.
exercises.why: **новый → новые** (acc. pl., agreeing with проблемы). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новые: A. anim. = G., inan. = N.. Ending -ые → -ые.  Declension (plural): новые · новых · новым · новые · новыми · новых.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Прилет самолета в Гонолулу намечен на ___ (завтрашнее утро, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: The airplane is scheduled to arrive at Honolulu tomorrow morning.
exercises.why: **утро → утро** (acc. sg.). Neuter, nominative singular in -о — declines like DLI's окно: A. окно. Ending -о → -о.  **завтрашний → завтрашнее** (acc. sg. n., agreeing with утро). Adjective type II, soft — declines like DLI's синий: A. anim. = G., inan. = N.. Ending -ее → -ее.  Declension: sg. утро · утра · утру · утро · утром · утре; pl. утра · утр · утрам · утра · утрами · утрах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: В ___ (какое время, acc. sg.) будет отлёт?
exercises.prompt: What time will the plane depart?
exercises.why: **время → время** (acc. sg.). Neuter, nominative singular in -мя — declines like DLI's имя: A. имя. Ending -я → -я.  **какой → какое** (acc. sg. n., agreeing with время). Adjective type III, guttural (after г, к, х) — declines like DLI's русский: A. anim. = G., inan. = N.. Ending -ое → -ое.  Declension: sg. время · времени · времени · время · временем · времени; pl. времена · времён · временам · времена · временами · временах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending -ой if stressed: новый — молодой; русский — плохой, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.» «The adjective «большой» belongs to the guttural type, in spite of its -ш-: большого, большому, большим, о большом.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Она исследует творчество братьев Гримм, потому что учится на ___ (литературовед, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: She is researching the Brothers Grimm, as she is a literature student.
exercises.why: **литературовед → литературоведа** (acc. sg.). Masculine, animate, nominative singular in a hard consonant — declines like DLI's студент: A. студента. Ending — (no ending) → -а.  Declension: sg. литературовед · литературоведа · литературоведу · литературоведа · литературоведом · литературоведе; pl. литературоведы · литературоведов · литературоведам · литературоведов · литературоведами · литературоведах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Никто ей в ___ (подмётка, acc. pl.) не годился.
exercises.prompt: No one could hold a candle to her.
exercises.why: **подмётка → подмётки** (acc. pl.). Feminine, inanimate; nominative plural подмётки; declines like DLI's книги (guttural stem): A. книги. Ending -а → -и.  Declension: sg. подмётка · подмётки · подмётке · подмётку · подмёткой · подмётке; pl. подмётки · подмёток · подмёткам · подмётки · подмётками · подмётках.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «The letter ы never follows г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, щ; therefore: книга — книги, река — реки, госпожа — госпожи.» — DLI, Lesson 23.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Цена на ___ (эта туфля, acc. pl.) снизилась.
exercises.prompt: The price of these shoes has been reduced.
exercises.why: **туфля → туфли** (acc. pl.). Feminine, inanimate; nominative plural туфли; declines like DLI's словари (soft stem): A. словари. Ending -я → -и.  **этот → эти** (acc. pl., agreeing with туфли). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новые: A. anim. = G., inan. = N.. Ending -эти → - (the stem changes: эти-).  Declension: sg. туфля · туфли · туфле · туфлю · туфлей · туфле; pl. туфли · туфель · туфлям · туфли · туфлями · туфлях.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).
